The verified ATT-0120 interface, confirmed by REV-0169 and REV-0170 and reflected in packet findings FND-0180 and FND-0185, identifies T_Z as ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6} minus Y;Q)(21)) and equivalently as the image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) in T. This uses Poincare-Verdier localization and weight strictness; it does not require a closed embedding of Z, a regular immersion, lci structure, or a Gysin map. The equivalence is correctly to the image, not to the full supports group, avoiding the FND-0168(3b) hazard.

The formal counterexample is valid. For X = A x P^{12} with A an abelian ninefold and Y = A x {pt}, codimension 12 support into the smooth 21-fold X can contribute H^2(A)(-12) in ordinary degree 26; after the Poincare twist (21) this is H^2(A)(9), pure of weight -16 and Borel-Moore degree 16, with off-diagonal Hodge types (-7,-9) and (-9,-7) in addition to (-8,-8). Thus purity, weight -16, Borel-Moore degree 16, and closed support inside a smooth 21-fold do not formally force a direct sum of Q(8).

The exact theorem excludes non-Tate cohomology of arbitrary bases, atlases, product models, or standalone Z unless a nonzero image in the named T_Z is proved. ATT-0126 correctly observes that the admitted standalone or product non-Tate classes do not constitute a disproof of the named T_Z. Packet finding FND-0186 additionally gives kernel vanishing for constant/product models whose classifying-image closure has dimension at most 2, and no general map from arbitrary atlas cohomology to T with proved nonzero image is supplied.

The required target_interface_reference object is present: interface_attempt_id is ATT-0120, interface_claim_ids are nonempty, and target_subquotient and target_map_use name the genuine ATT-0120 kernel and inclusion. However, the substantive contract is not met: survival_or_tate_argument explicitly states that no unconditional Tate or survival argument is available. Therefore the interface reference names the correct object but does not prove the assigned theorem rather than a surrogate cohomology result.

The assigned statement that this named T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8) is neither proved nor disproved by ATT-0126. The attempt's own gap marker records that the Hodge type of im(W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) -> T) is undetermined on residual support strata of dimensions 9 through 16, and no admitted artifact proves that every non-Tate summand either is absent from the source or dies in the map to T.

finding_candidates.rationale: Reusable blocking principle for future C66-TATE-SUPPORT attempts: the verified interface's purity and weight ledger cannot be upgraded to Tate type without additional geometry.
finding_candidates.statement: For a smooth complex stack or scheme X of dimension d and a closed support Y, the corner image W_{-k}H^{BM}_k(Y;Q) -> W_{-k}H^{BM}_k(X;Q) can be pure of weight -k and nonzero without being Tate. In particular, for X = A x P^{12} with A an abelian ninefold and Y = A x {pt}, the codimension-12 supported corner contains H^2(A)(9) of weight -16 with Hodge types (-7,-9), (-8,-8), and (-9,-7). Thus any C66-TATE-SUPPORT argument must supply genuine geometric control, such as support dimension at most 8, Tate strata, or killing of non-Tate summands in the map to T; purity, degree, weight, and closed support are insufficient.

finding_candidates.rationale: Additional evidence for packet-visible finding FND-0189: correct population of target_interface_reference fields is not itself a discharge of the unconditional Tate theorem.
finding_candidates.statement: ATT-0126 populates target_interface_reference with the genuine ATT-0120 interface: interface_attempt_id ATT-0120, interface_claim_ids CLM-0120-2 through CLM-0120-7, target_subquotient T_Z = ker(r_T) = im(W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) -> T), and target_map_use the verified inclusion phi. Nevertheless its survival_or_tate_argument explicitly states that no unconditional Tate or survival argument is available. This is another witness that schema population of the interface fields is not a substantive discharge of C66-TATE-SUPPORT; the named source, map, and subquotient must actually yield the Tate conclusion with no undischarged hypothesis.

Poincare duality identification T = W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) is used with the correct degree/weight/twist arithmetic: ordinary degree 26, dimension 21, twist 21, giving Borel-Moore degree 16 and weight -16. No integral-coefficient or coarse-moduli variant is used.

The required unconditional geometric input proving Tate type of the named T_Z is absent. Possible sufficient inputs would include Tate type of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q), stratum-by-stratum Tate control of the residual support, support dimension at most 8, or a proof that every non-Tate summand of the source maps to zero in T. ATT-0126 correctly records that none of these is supplied by ATT-0120 or its confirmations.

strongest_attack: Strongest attack: attempt to force the Tate conclusion from the verified ATT-0120 interface using only purity, weight -16, Borel-Moore degree 16, and closed support inside the smooth 21-fold M_{6,6}. This attack fails, and ATT-0126 correctly shows why: Poincare-Verdier localization only identifies T_Z as a pure polarizable weight -16 subobject/image; it does not determine Hodge bidegrees. The abelian-ninefold example A x {pt} in A x P^{12} exhibits off-diagonal types (-7,-9) and (-9,-7) in the same corner, so no formal Poincare twist, semisimplicity, Kunneth shift, or Gysin bookkeeping yields Q(8). Conversely, the strongest disproof attack using packet product-model non-Tate classes such as FND-0176/FND-0178 also fails under the exact theorem statement, because those classes live in arbitrary bases or standalone models and have no proved nonzero image in the named T_Z; constant/product closures can even have zero kernel by FND-0186. Stack-versus-coarse, rational-versus-integral, and invariants-versus-coinvariants hazards are avoided by the Q-coefficient stack-level interface, but avoiding those hazards does not supply the missing Tate input. Outcome: the exact theorem remains unresolved; the attempt is candid about this, so the verdict is incomplete rather than refuted. Evidence limitation: no web evidence was available; the review uses only the supplied local task artifacts.
theorem_statement: Let T_Z be the canonical mixed-Hodge subquotient of T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) supplied by a verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum. Prove T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8). A disproof must exhibit a non-Tate subquotient of this named T_Z through the verified target interface; non-Tate cohomology of an arbitrary family base, atlas, product model, standalone Z, or a source class whose target image is not proved nonzero is not a disproof. This theorem does not itself assemble the complementary target terms.
